summary: This article explains how two tectonic plates slowly pulling apart carved a huge valley across East Africa, filled it with deep lakes and volcanoes, and may someday split the continent in two.
introduce: Read the title “The Great Rift Valley” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: having to do with the huge moving plates that make up Earth's outer layer
a long crack or split that opens where land is pulling apart
a long, deep, narrow dip cut into the ground or seafloor

challengeTerms.def: describes two things, such as tectonic plates, moving steadily away from each other
hot melted rock found below Earth's surface
a long, steep slope or cliff that separates two areas of different height

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a landscape that looks solid and unchanging today could actually be slowly transforming over millions of years? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain the steps that create the Great Rift Valley, from moving plates to the finished trench.
struggling: Pre-teach tectonic, rift, and trench with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use divergent, magma, and escarpment in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
